reviews.why: BHP and Escondida's supervisors' union reached a new three-year agreement on October 14, 2026, averting the strike the union had called days earlier, so the disruption path that would have deepened the supply gap did not happen this week. Copper traded at $6.53 per pound on October 16, 2026, well above the $6.15 kill level, and the restart-pace question central to the original thesis still waits on BHP's October 21 quarterly operational review.

no_new_call_note: A pass across commodities, crypto and stocks this week turned up disputed labor negotiations at a second mine, an unchanged OPEC+ output decision, and a rare-earth restriction already reported since September -- nothing new, confirmed by more than one independent source, and still ahead of what the market already expects, so no new call opens this week.
